approval.cost: Connection tiers (per app, effective 2 March 2026 per the pricing pages in force): Starter, maximum 5 connections, no charge, no payment method; Core, maximum 50 connections, $35 AUD/month; Plus, maximum 1,000 connections, $245 AUD/month, prerequisite App Certification; Advanced, maximum 10,000 connections, $1,445 AUD/month, prerequisites App Certification AND Security Assessment (initial and annual); Enterprise, no limit, price on application, App Certification + Security Assessment, App Store listing required. Egress allowances: ingress unlimited on all tiers; egress included 10 GB (Core), 50 GB (Plus), 250 GB (Advanced), overage $2.40 AUD per GB; allowances reset on the first of the calendar month (UTC); a registered credit card is required from Core upward. 'Connection count and API data consumption via the Xero API is measured and priced at the app level. Apps cannot share connection counts or API volume used, even if they are from the same developer.' Custom Connections (the alternative flavor) are priced per connection ($10/mo AUD inc GST, $10 NZD, £5 GBP, $5 USD) and excluded from the tier model
approval.trigger: No review is required before external users can start connecting: a new app can connect real customer organisations immediately, but it is hard-capped by its pricing tier (Starter: 5 connections). Review enters through App Certification, the gate for scale and for the App Store, not for first connections: 'you'll need ten [customers] to get certified', certification is a prerequisite for Plus and above ('Apps on Plus, Advanced and Enterprise must be certified'), and 'The Xero App Store only lists Xero-certified apps... Every app must meet Xero requirements and review it against a list of certification checkpoints.' Listed apps must also implement Sign Up with Xero. A per-organisation cap compounds this: 'an org can have 2 uncertified apps plus as many custom connection apps as needed', so an individual customer can only connect to two uncertified apps in total until you certify. Premium gate: 'The Journals endpoint, Xero Practice Manager API, and Bulk Connections require a security assessment (initial and annual) and use case approval, and they are only available starting at the Advanced tier.' To add a 6th connection you must first add payment details and move to the Core tier.
approval.wait: Not stated (no certification review duration or SLA in the official pages read)

blockers.detail: Without the offline_access scope no refresh token is issued, and since access tokens live only 30 minutes, the connection effectively dies half an hour after consent.
blockers.howToClear: Always include offline_access in the authorization request.
blockers.title: offline_access is make-or-break

blockers.detail: You need ten customers to certify, but before certification you are capped at 5 (Starter) or 50 (Core) connections AND each customer organisation can hold only 2 uncertified apps. Plan the path to 10 live connections early.
blockers.howToClear: Move to Core early, prioritize customers whose organisations have an uncertified slot free, and start the certification checkpoint work before hitting the cap.
blockers.title: Certification chicken-and-egg

blockers.detail: 'If you remove a broad scope from an existing connection, you won't be able to re-add it. Any broad scope you remove will be permanently replaced by granular scopes.' Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 use the new granular scopes; pre-existing apps 'will have until September 2027 to move from broad scopes to granular scopes', and new connections from 29 April 2026 use granular scopes (which don't include journal access; Journals moved behind the Advanced-tier premium gate). Changing scopes requires the user to reauthorize with explicit consent.
blockers.howToClear: Map your broad scopes to granular equivalents deliberately and treat removal as permanent.
blockers.title: Granular-scope migration is a one-way door

alternatives: Custom Connection (client credentials grant; one organisation per connection, authorized by a named authorising user via an email-guided consent flow; 'Goodbye refresh tokens'; a paid add-on purchased by the organisation, available in AU, NZ, UK and US only; suitable for bespoke/single-client integrations, not multi-tenant SaaS onboarding)

flavor.recommended: A Web app in the Xero Developer Portal using the authorization code flow, with the offline_access scope
flavor.why: The object is an app created in the Xero Developer Portal (My Apps > New app), issuing a Client ID; a Client Secret is generated from the app's Configuration. 'The Xero API does not support basic API Key authentication. Our API uses OAuth 2.0 which means you need to register your app to get a client id and client secret.' OAuth 1.0a still exists but 'is in the process of being deprecated and OAuth 2.0 is required for all new integrations'. After authorization you call GET api.xero.com/connections to learn which organisations (tenants) the user connected, and every API call carries the access token plus an xero-tenant-id header. Scopes are requested per-authorization; Xero is mid-migration from broad scopes to granular scopes (accounting.invoices, accounting.payments, and similar).

name: Xero
nuances: Refresh behavior: 'All Xero access tokens expire after 30 minutes.' 'Unused refresh tokens expire after 60 days. If you don't refresh your access token within 60 days the user will need to reauthorise your app.' Rotation grace: 'If you don't receive a response from a token refresh you can retry using your existing refresh token for up to 30 minutes.' Replace the stored refresh token with the new one returned on every refresh.

Tenant handling: one token set can cover several organisations, but every API call must specify which one via the xero-tenant-id header. An organisation can only be connected to a given app once. 'The user that connects the integration has to have either Standard, Adviser, or Administrator level user with the Connected Apps permission. The API essentially works on behalf of the user that authorised it to connect' (e.g. Reporting APIs need the authorising user to have Reports access; Payroll APIs require a Payroll Admin).

Rate limits (official FAQ): per tenant, Concurrent Limit 5 calls in progress, Minute Limit 60 calls per minute, Daily Limit 1,000 calls per day for Starter, 5,000 for higher tiers; App Minute Limit 10,000 calls per minute across all tenants. Responses include X-DayLimit-Remaining, X-MinLimit-Remaining and X-AppMinLimit-Remaining headers; exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After. Up to 50 redirect URIs per app; wildcards are not supported.

Under-scoped calls return 'a 401 forbidden error with a response header WWW-Authenticate: insufficent_scope' [sic]. 'If you choose to make changes to your custom connection it will be deactivated until it is re-authorised' (Custom Connections).

AI-specific prohibition, material for an AI-agent SaaS: Xero's updated Developer Terms clarify that 'API data may not be used to train AI/ML models', and that 'apps must not use bots or browser extensions to undermine our security controls or simulate user actions'. There are no separate sandbox credentials: testing uses the Demo Company with the same app.
prerequisites: A free Xero account (and the Demo Company for development)
Company/application URL and OAuth 2.0 redirect URI(s) for app creation
A tier plan: payment details for Core and above; ten live customers for certification

steps.detail: 'The first step is to sign up for a free Xero account.' For development, use the Demo Company (recommended) or start a trial or paid Xero organisation subscription.
steps.title: Sign up for a free Xero account

steps.detail: Developer Portal > My Apps > New app: app name, integration type Web app, company/application URL and OAuth 2.0 redirect URI(s), and accept the Xero Developer Platform Terms and Conditions. Open the app's Configuration, note the Client ID, and click 'Generate a secret' for the Client Secret.
steps.title: Create the app (Web app); generate a secret

steps.detail: Send the user to login.xero.com/identity/connect/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope (including offline_access, plus openid/profile/email if needed), and state. The user signs in, selects the organisation(s) to connect, and consents; each organisation goes through the standard OAuth consent step.
steps.title: Build the authorization URL (include offline_access)

steps.detail: Exchange the code at identity.xero.com/connect/token for the token set (access token, ID token if openid requested, refresh token if offline_access requested). Then GET api.xero.com/connections with the access token and store each tenantId alongside the token set.
steps.title: Exchange the code; resolve tenants

steps.detail: Call APIs with Authorization: Bearer and xero-tenant-id: <tenantId> on every request. Access tokens expire after 30 minutes.
steps.title: Call APIs per tenant

steps.detail: Before the access token expires, exchange the refresh token for a new token set and replace the stored refresh token with the new one returned. Refresh at least every 60 days or the user must reauthorize.
steps.title: Refresh proactively (60-day inactivity expiry)

steps.detail: New apps start on Starter (max 5 connections). 'In order to add a 6th connection, you will need to first add your payment details. Once that is complete, you will move to the Core tier' (max 50, $35 AUD/month). Plus (1,000) requires App Certification (ten customers); Advanced (10,000) adds a Security Assessment (initial and annual); Enterprise is unlimited with App Store listing required. Apply in the Developer Portal.
steps.title: Scale: tiers and App Certification

tagline: No review to start connecting, but scale is the product: connection tiers cap you at 5 (free), 50, 1,000, or 10,000 organisations, App Certification (which needs ten customers) gates the upper tiers, and each customer organisation can only hold two uncertified apps. Tokens live 30 minutes; refresh tokens die after 60 days unused.

time.active: ~15 min of portal setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Same day for the first 5 connections; scaling is a tier + certification program with no stated review duration
